title.en: Evaluate the effect of policies by 1990

say.en: If foreign cars are cheaper and better, will a new Indian car maker survive? Planners of the 1950 seconds answered by shutting out imports. In this lesson: Explain import substitution.
Distinguish tariffs and quotas.
Evaluate the effect of policies by 1990.

body.en: India followed an *inward-looking trade strategy* called import substitution: replacing imports with domestic production. Domestic industries were protected from foreign competition by tariffs, which are taxes on imported goods, and quotas, which fix the quantity of goods that can be imported.
body.kn: ಭಾರತ ಆಮದು ಪರ್ಯಾಯ ಎಂಬ ಒಳಮುಖ ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ನೀತಿ ಅನುಸರಿಸಿತು: ಆಮದಿನ ಬದಲು ದೇಶೀಯ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ. ಸುಂಕ (ಆಮದಿನ ಮೇಲಿನ ತೆರಿಗೆ) ಮತ್ತು ಕೋಟಾ (ಆಮದು ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ ಮಿತಿ) ಮೂಲಕ ದೇಶೀಯ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಲಾಯಿತು.

title.en: On the board: Protection by tariff

say.en: A machine costs 1 lakh rupees abroad. A 60 per cent tariff is added at the border.
The Indian maker sells at 1.4 lakh, so the buyer chooses the domestic machine.
Industry's share in GDP rose from 11.8 per cent in 1950-51 to 24.6 per cent in 1990-91.
But protection bred inefficiency, losses in public firms and the permit licence raj.
On the board: Protection by tariff.

caption.en: A good can be imported at the world price of ₹40. A tariff raises the price inside India: home producers sell more, buyers buy less, and imports shrink. At 37.5% imports stop altogether. Prices and quantities are illustrative.
caption.kn: ವಿಶ್ವ ಬೆಲೆ ₹40. ಸುಂಕ ದೇಶದೊಳಗಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಏರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ದೇಶೀಯ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕರು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಮಾರುತ್ತಾರೆ, ಕೊಳ್ಳುವವರು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ, ಆಮದು ಕುಗ್ಗುತ್ತದೆ. 37.5% ನಲ್ಲಿ ಆಮದು ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Industry's share in GDP rose from 11.8 per cent in 1950-51 to 24.6 per cent in 1990-91, and industry grew at about 6 per cent a year. Industry diversified, and protection helped electronics and automobiles develop. But many public sector firms made losses, the licence system ("permit licence raj") let big firms block competitors, and protection made producers less efficient and less concerned about quality.
body.kn: ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಯ ಪಾಲು 1950-51ರಲ್ಲಿ 11.8% ರಿಂದ 1990-91ರಲ್ಲಿ 24.6%ಕ್ಕೆ ಏರಿತು. ಆದರೆ ಅನೇಕ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳು ನಷ್ಟ ಅನುಭವಿಸಿದವು ಮತ್ತು ಪರವಾನಗಿ ರಾಜ್ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆಯನ್ನು ಕುಗ್ಗಿಸಿತು.

problem.en: A machine costs ₹1,00,000 abroad. India puts a 60% tariff on it. A domestic maker sells the same machine at ₹1,40,000. Which will a buyer choose, and why?

steps.en: The buyer chooses the domestic machine: the tariff protects the domestic producer.

answer.en: The domestic machine (₹1,40,000 < ₹1,60,000): this is how tariffs supported import substitution.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A machine costs ₹1,00,000 abroad. India puts a 60% tariff on it. A domestic maker sells the same machine at ₹1,40,000. Which will a buyer choose, and why?

say.en: Let us work through this together. A machine costs 1,00,000 rupees abroad. India puts a 60 percent tariff on it. A domestic maker sells the same machine at 1,40,000 rupees. Which will a buyer choose, and why?
Imported price with tariff equals 1,00,000 times 1.60 equals 1,60,000 rupees.
Domestic price equals 1,40,000, rupees which is lower.
The buyer chooses the domestic machine: the tariff protects the domestic producer.
So the answer is The domestic machine (1,40,000 rupees is less than 1,60,000 rupees): this is how tariffs supported import substitution.

List II: I Fixed quantity of a good that can be imported II Permission needed to start or expand a firm III Tax on imported goods IV Replacing imports with domestic production.
